source_title: Suspected scaphoid injuries managed by MRI direct from the emergency department: a single-centre prospective cohort study
locator: Results; MRI findings among patients who completed MRI (n=208).
source_setting: Single-centre UK emergency department MRI pathway; patients aged 12+ with suspected scaphoid fracture and normal scaphoid-series radiographs after clinical assessment.
source_period: Prospective cohort enrollment: end September 2018 through end September 2019; minimum one-year outcome follow-up, EHR searched January 2021; article published 2021.
source_n: 208 completed MRI scans; 258 referred from 337 assessed.
quantity: MRI-detected occult scaphoid fracture among completed scans
unit: patients; source-reported percent and separately calculated percent
source_evidence_basis: Prospective service evaluation reports 27 scaphoid fractures among 208 completed scans (reported 13%).
limitations: Selected patients referred based on examination and radiograph review; single centre; ages 12+ (not adult-only); MRI completion denominator differs from 258 referred. This is not an unconditional probability for all wrist injuries or all negative radiographs.
inferred_scenario_use: Calibration comparator only for a clinician-selected suspected-scaphoid subgroup sent for MRI; do not transfer to all negative wrist films or treat as an RWJ estimate.

source_title: Suspected scaphoid injuries managed by MRI direct from the emergency department: a single-centre prospective cohort study
locator: Results; MRI findings among 208 completed scans.
source_setting: Single-centre UK emergency department MRI pathway; selected suspected scaphoid injuries with negative radiographs.
source_period: Prospective cohort enrollment: end September 2018 through end September 2019; minimum one-year outcome follow-up, EHR searched January 2021; article published 2021.
quantity: Alternative or no abnormality MRI findings
source_evidence_basis: Full-text Results gives six MRI outcome categories among 208: scaphoid fracture 27, other fracture 45, scaphoid contusion 13, other contusion/ligament injury 42, degenerative only 21, normal 60. Counts sum to 208; the 27 scaphoid fractures were omitted from the earlier value list.
limitations: Mutually exclusive MRI outcome categories reported in the Results sum to 208; separate Table III describes concurrent associated injuries, so these category counts should not be conflated with that table. Selected pathway referrals, patients aged 12+, and single-centre setting limit transfer.
inferred_scenario_use: Use as a distributional external comparator for MRI-result branches after clinician-selected imaging; retain separate occult fracture, other injury, and normal outcomes.

source_title: Suspected scaphoid injuries managed by MRI direct from the emergency department: a single-centre prospective cohort study
locator: Results; ED discharge and re-presentation after MRI.
source_setting: Single-centre UK emergency department MRI pathway; selected patients with suspected scaphoid injury.
source_period: Prospective enrollment end September 2018 through end September 2019; minimum one-year outcomes; EHR searched January 2021.
source_n: 100 of 208 completed-MRI patients discharged by ED with advice; at least one year outcome follow-up and EHR search in January 2021.
unit: patients; reported count, not a time-standardized probability
source_evidence_basis: Full-text Methods state outcomes/complications were recorded at minimum one year and electronic patient records searched January 2021; Results report 100 MRI patients discharged by ED with advice and one re-presentation.
limitations: Single-centre selected cohort; return ascertainment used hospital electronic records, and exact index date for the 100 discharges is not specified. Re-presentation is not equivalent to missed fracture or failed follow-up.
inferred_scenario_use: May inform a qualitative return branch only; do not encode as a calibrated unplanned-return probability without defined follow-up horizon and comparable ascertainment.

source_title: Clinical and cost implications of using immediate MRI in the management of patients with a suspected scaphoid fracture and negative radiographs: results from the SMaRT trial
locator: Abstract and Methods; randomized trial, initial MRI versus control follow-up.
source_setting: UK ED randomized trial; age at least 16, clinical history/exam consistent with suspected scaphoid fracture, negative initial four-view radiographs; exclusions included confirmed injury and out-of-catchment patients.
source_period: Published 2019; enrollment dates not stated in inspected abstract excerpt.
source_n: 136 randomized (68 per arm); 4 participants were lost to follow-up; analysis denominators at three months were 65 control and 67 intervention. Five intervention participants did not receive MRI.
quantity: Scaphoid fracture diagnosis by 3 months, MRI arm versus control
source_evidence_basis: Full-text Results report scaphoid fractures diagnosed up to three months: 4/65 control and 7/67 intervention (reported 6.2% and 10.4%). Five intervention participants did not undergo MRI; four participants withdrew and were lost to follow-up.
limitations: Randomized workflow comparison, not an untreated natural-history estimate. MRI-arm denominator requires caution because five randomized participants did not receive MRI; follow-up imaging differed by arm. Adult-only age threshold was 16, so population includes older adolescents.
inferred_scenario_use: Use only to compare trial pathway outcomes under its eligibility and follow-up process; do not interpret arm difference as causal probability for an individual or as local prevalence.

source_title: Cost and clinical effectiveness of MRI in occult scaphoid fractures: a randomised controlled trial
locator: PubMed abstract; 84 ED patients randomized to early MRI or clinic reassessment.
source_setting: UK district general hospital ED; suspected occult scaphoid fracture; MRI arm early wrist MRI and discharge if no injury, control clinic reassessment.
source_period: Published 2013 (online 2012); recruitment dates not stated in abstract.
quantity: Mean clinic appointments during study follow-up
unit: clinic appointments per participant; mean ± SD
source_evidence_basis: Inspected PubMed abstract reports fewer mean clinic appointments in MRI group; it also reports scaphoid fracture 3/45 (6.7%) versus 4/39 (10.3%).
limitations: Small single-centre RCT; abstract does not supply a detailed follow-up duration for appointment count. Appointment burden is not probability of referral, failed follow-up, or return visit.
inferred_scenario_use: Use as an external pathway utilization comparator only. Do not infer that MRI causes fewer ED returns or that this rate transfers to local practice.

source_title: Prospective comparison of magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography in diagnosing occult scaphoid fractures
locator: PubMed abstract; patients with negative radiographs and negative CT underwent MRI.
source_setting: Prospective diagnostic cohort; suspected scaphoid fracture after wrist trauma; CT after two negative radiographs at 7-10 days, followed by MRI for eligible CT-negative patients.
source_period: Published 2023; recruitment dates not stated in abstract.
source_n: 100 included patients with negative radiographs and CT.
quantity: MRI findings after negative radiographs and CT

scaphoid_fracture.denominator_status: Abstract says of these fractures; intended denominator is ambiguous.

fracture_or_bruise_referred_hand_surgery.reported_rate: 25% of patients with fractures and bone bruising; numerator and denominator not given

source_evidence_basis: Abstract reports MRI fractures in 16% of 100 patients (15 patients), scaphoid fracture 8%, bone bruising 10%, and hand-surgery referral for 25% of patients with fracture/bone bruising. The 15/100 count calculates to 15%, inconsistent with the abstract’s 16%; both source wording and count are preserved without resolving the discrepancy.
limitations: Selected CT-negative second-line cohort. Abstract percentage/count conflict for any fracture (16% versus 15/100); hand-surgery referral numerator and denominator are not specified. Keep those quantities uncalibrated pending full paper. Scaphoid percentage wording does not establish an 8/100 count. Do not infer subgroup numerators from rounded percentages.
inferred_scenario_use: Calibration only for a second-line CT-negative pathway; keep separate from initial negative-radiograph scenarios and do not infer universal hand-surgery referral.

source_title: Suspected scaphoid injuries managed by MRI direct from the emergency department: a single-centre prospective cohort study
locator: Abstract Results; Table I, referred for MRI columns
source_setting: Single-centre UK emergency department MRI pathway; patients aged 12+ with suspected scaphoid fracture and normal scaphoid-series radiographs after clinical assessment.
source_period: Prospective cohort enrollment: end September 2018 through end September 2019; minimum one-year outcome follow-up, EHR searched January 2021; article published 2021.
source_n: 258 referred for MRI; 208 completed, 45 did not attend, 5 did not tolerate the scan
quantity: MRI completion and reasons for noncompletion among referred patients
source_evidence_basis: Original cohort reports 208 completed scans among 258 referrals, with 45 nonattendances and five patients unable to tolerate MRI.
limitations: Single selected UK referral pathway, ages 12 and older. MRI nonattendance is not failure of all subsequent follow-up or an RWJ scheduling probability. No common referral-to-scan censoring window is established here.
inferred_scenario_use: Separate completed, not attended and not tolerated imaging branches for scenario authoring; do not silently omit the 50 noncompleters when interpreting MRI yield.
